content: The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem node with **gray/white fluffy cottony mycelium** growth at the joint. Background leaves are yellowed. This strongly suggests White Mold or possibly Rhizoctonia. Let me compare reference images.

- All other candidates ruled out:

  - Diaporthe/Phomopsis: stem/pod cankers with pycnidia, no cotton
  - Phytophthora: brown stem canker near soil, no fluffy growth
  - Fusarium/Pythium: root rot symptoms
  - All leaf-disease classes (Frogeye, Septoria, etc.): not stem mycelium

The gray-white cottony mycelium at the stem node is the defining characteristic of **White Mold** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum).
